x.intro: N'Djamena (pron. en-jah-may-nah) is the capital of Chad. It is by far the country's largest city, with a population of 1 million people. It lies directly on the border of Cameroon, and is on the confluence of the Chari and Logone rivers. The city has been at the centre of many heated rebellions and revolts, and in February 2008 was entered by rebel troops.

x.intro: Abeche is the capital of Ouaddai Province in Chad. It was once the capital of the Wadai Empire.

must.d: Former capital of the Wadai Empire. It has been deserted since its wells went dry in the late 19th century and the capital was moved to Abéché. Situated between hills, it is still home to a ruined palace, mosque and city wall.

must.d: A massive shield volcano, Emi Koussi is the tallest mountain in Chad and in the entire Sahara, its summit towering 3 km above the surrounding sandstone plains.

x.around: If you rent a vehicle you can self-drive in the park with a ranger. Otherwise, twice-daily game drives are included in the lodge pricing.
x.intro: Zakouma National Park is a 3,000-km² protected area in the south of Chad. Since management of the park was taken over by African Parks, in partnership with the Chadian government, this park has seen a resurgence of wildlife and has brought tourism to a beautifully unique but rarely visited part of the world.
x.safe: Photography is not allowed in public places in Chad, and be particularly careful in the airport with cameras and phones. Zakouma has special permission for photography within the park though.
